name: Queens River Campground
note: Boise NF (Idaho City RD) at the Middle Fork Boise River near the Queens River trailhead (FS Rd 206), between Arrowrock Reservoir and Atlanta; 4 primitive sites, no potable water, vault toilet, first-come first-served. Access via narrow, rough FS Rd 268 (~62 mi) — the same road serving Riverside/Power Plant; small, best for compact rigs. --Claude

name: North Shore Campground (Alturas Lake)
note: On the north shore of Alturas Lake, Sawtooth NRA. 10 single + 4 double sites, vault toilets, no hookups; first-come, first-served (not on recreation.gov). Mixed-conifer setting, RV-capable (no big-rig length posted). --Claude

name: Montour Campground
note: Bureau of Reclamation land in the Montour WMA (managed by Idaho Fish & Game), adjacent to the Payette River above Black Canyon Reservoir, ~5 mi NE of Emmett. ~12-18 primitive back-in sites (max ~25-32 ft), vault toilets, potable water, RV dump station; $8/night, first-come, first-served, seasonal. --Claude

name: Graham Bridge Campground
note: Small Boise NF campground on the Middle Fork Boise River near Atlanta. 6 first-come, first-served developed sites, vault toilet, seasonal water, no hookups; RVs allowed (no length posted). Gravel forest-road (drive-in) access. --Claude

name: Hot Springs Campground
note: Boise NF, Banks-Lowman Hwy east of Garden Valley on the South Fork Payette River; 8 single sites (first-come, first-served) plus 3 reservable group sites, paved spurs, vault toilets, drinking water, no hookups; natural hot springs across the road. Group sites reservable online. --Claude

name: Park Creek Campground (Lowman)
note: Boise NF, off FS Road 582 (Clear Creek Rd) ~4 mi north of Lowman at the Park/Clear Creek confluence; 24 sites in two reservable group loops (Rainbow 1-12, Trout 13-24) plus additional single sites first-come, first-served when the group loops aren't booked. Vault toilets, drinking water, no hookups; good trout fishing. --Claude

name: Mt. Heyburn Campground
note: USFS campground on the east side of Redfish Lake in the Sawtooth NRA; 19 single sites, no hookups, potable water, vault toilet. First-come, first-served only (Scan & Pay). Accessed via Forest Rd 214 south of Stanley. --Claude

name: Sockeye Campground
note: USFS campground on the shore of Redfish Lake in the Sawtooth NRA; 23 sites incl 6 doubles scattered through lodgepole pine, no hookups, water and toilets. First-come, first-served only (Scan & Pay). --Claude

name: Grandjean Campground
note: 31-site USFS campground in old-growth ponderosa near the Sawtooth Wilderness boundary along the South Fork Payette River; vault toilets, potable water, no hookups. All sites first-come, first-served (Scan & Pay); 10 sites designated for horse campers. Access is a narrow one-lane dirt road (FR 824) ~20 min in, tight in spots, best for tents and smaller rigs -- a compact 23-ft rig fits the few trailer-capable sites but big rigs should use caution. --Claude

name: Chinook Bay Campground
note: 13-site USFS campground on the north shore of Little Redfish Lake in the Sawtooth NRA, ~3 mi S of Stanley off Redfish Lake Rd; lodgepole pine, flush toilets, potable water, no hookups, accommodates tents/trailers/RVs. All sites first-come, first-served; non-motorized lake. Fills quickly in peak season. --Claude

name: Iron Creek Campground
note: 9-site USFS campground on Iron Creek in the Sawtooth NRA SW of Stanley (off Hwy 21 via Iron Creek Rd), a trailhead base for the Sawtooth Wilderness (Sawtooth Lake, Alice Lake); lodgepole pine, potable water, primitive/limited toilets, no hookups. All sites first-come, first-served; loop A and a couple of loop B sites fit larger rigs including a 23-ft RV. --Claude

name: Nip and Tuck Road Dispersed Camping
note: Dispersed camping along Nip & Tuck Rd (FR 633) in the Sawtooth NF on the ridge NW of Stanley, with sweeping Sawtooth Range and Stanley views; no water, toilets, or amenities, 10-day max stay, first-come, first-served. Larger RVs limited to the lower, more-level sections off Hwy 21 just past the bridge (a 23-ft rig fits there); upper road is narrow, rutted and off-camber. Do NOT approach from the Hwy 75 (east) end -- a deep wash can damage low-clearance vehicles. --Claude

name: Holman Creek Campground
note: Sawtooth NF campground on the Salmon River (Salmon River Recreation Complex) east of Stanley toward Clayton. 10 sites incl 1 double; vault toilets, potable water. First-come, first-served (Scan & Pay onsite). End turnaround is small for very large RVs but a 23-ft rig fits. --Claude

name: Rattlesnake Campground
note: Boise NF (Emmett RD) campground on the Middle Fork Payette River, ~14 mi N of Crouch on FR-698; 11 single sites + 1 group site (to 100 people), RVs up to 35 ft, potable water, vault toilets, no hookups. Reservable online (group and singles); individual sites FCFS when unreserved. --Claude

name: Summit Creek Recreation Site
note: BLM (Challis Field Office) primitive recreation site by Summit Creek and Summit Reservoir, ~50 mi NW of Howe via county road + Summit Rd (gravel); ~7 sites with picnic tables and vault toilets, no potable water. First-come, first-served, 14-day limit. Satellite shows open drive-in clearings by the creek. --Claude

name: Trail Creek Campground
note: Boise NF (Emmett RD) campground on the Middle Fork Payette River, ~17 mi N of Garden Valley on FR-698/NF-698; 12 sites (several pull-through) accommodating RVs up to 35 ft, hand-pump well water, 2 vault toilets, no hookups. First-come, first-served, ~$12/night. --Claude

name: Flat Rock Campground
note: Salmon-Challis NF, on the Yankee Fork of the Salmon River ~2 mi up FR-013 from Sunbeam Dam (Hwy 75). 6 drive-in sites, vault toilet, hand-pump water, no hookups; trailers/motorhomes to 32 ft. First-come, first-served (self-pay). Historic Yankee Fork gold-dredge district nearby. --Claude

name: Pole Flat Campground
note: Salmon-Challis NF, ~3 mi up FR-013 (Yankee Fork Rd) from Sunbeam, on a bench above the Salmon River/Yankee Fork dredge ponds. 10 drive-in tent/RV sites, vault toilet, drinking water, no hookups; trailers/motorhomes to 32 ft. First-come, first-served (self-pay). --Claude

name: Sheep Trail Campground
note: Sawtooth NRA (Sawtooth NF), adjacent to Hwy 21 ~10 mi W of Stanley in the Cape Horn/Marsh Creek area. One reservable group site made up of four smaller drive-in sites; when the group isn't booked the individual sites are FCFS. Vault toilet, hand-pump water, no hookups. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Hollywood Campground
note: On the east shore of Sage Hen Reservoir, Boise NF (Emmett RD), ~4,800 ft; reached via FS gravel roads from Ola. Single-family drive-in sites, vault toilets, boat ramp/dock; mix of reservable (recreation.gov) and first-come, first-served. Currently closed for reconstruction and being modernized to add more RV camping, campsites and a toilet, reopening ~Nov 2026; season mid-May-end of Sept. --Claude

name: Silver Creek Plunge
note: Private hot-springs resort in Peace Valley, Boise NF; ~15 mi of gravel forest road (FSR 671) from Crouch, road open to all vehicles. First-come, first-served tent/RV sites, no hookups (limited solar power), hot-springs pool and general store. Also manages the adjacent USFS Silver Creek Campground. --Claude

name: Silver Creek Campground
note: In Peace Valley along Silver Creek, Boise NF; ~25 mi N of Garden Valley via gravel forest road. 53-59 nonelectric single-family sites in three loops (Valley Creek, Lower/Upper Peace Creek) plus two group sites; paved roads and paved parking spurs, drinking water, vault toilets. Individual sites first-come, first-served (register/pay at Silver Creek Plunge store); group sites reservable online. --Claude

name: Cartwright Ridge Campground
note: On Sage Hen Reservoir, Boise NF (Emmett RD), ~4,800 ft; reached via FS gravel roads from Ola. Small campground (~5 single-family drive-in sites), vault toilet, no potable water; reservable via recreation.gov with some first-come, first-served. Boating/fishing, boat ramp nearby; open mid-May-end of Sept (listed Site Open, 2026). --Claude

name: Sage Hen Creek Campground
note: On the NE shore of Sage Hen Reservoir, Boise NF (Emmett RD), ~4,800 ft; reached via FS gravel roads from Ola. ~9 single-family drive-in sites (SAGE loop), vault toilets, hand-pump drinking water, boat ramp/dock; mix of reservable (recreation.gov) and first-come, first-served. Was closed for reconstruction through 6/30/2026 (now reopened); season mid-May-end of Sept. --Claude

name: Antelope Campground
note: On Sage Hen Reservoir, Boise NF (Emmett RD), ~4,800 ft; reached via FS gravel roads from Ola. 13 single-family drive-in sites with paved/gravel parking spurs plus a tent-only group site (to 30 people); reservable + first-come, first-served via recreation.gov. Currently closed for reconstruction, being modernized to add more RV camping, sites and a toilet, reopening ~late 2026; season mid-May-end of Sept. --Claude

name: West End Campground
note: Caribou-Targhee NF drive-in dispersed camping area on the west shore of Island Park Reservoir, reached via Green Canyon Rd (~9.5 mi gravel from Harriman SP). Undeveloped sites (no toilets/water/trash), boat ramp on site; first-come, first-served, 14-day limit. --Claude

name: Box Canyon Campground
note: Caribou-Targhee NF (Ashton/Island Park RD) on the rim above the Henrys Fork of the Snake River, ~1 mi S of the Island Park Ranger Station off US-20. 16 single + 2 double sites incl 2 pull-throughs, tables/fire rings/grills, vault toilets, drinking water; gravel roads accommodate RVs to ~40 ft. First-come, first-served, late May-early Sept. --Claude

name: Mann Creek Campground
note: Payette NF at Mann Creek Reservoir, ~15 mi N of Weiser via Hwy 95 and Mann Creek Rd. 13 sites (6 reservable, rest FCFS), vault toilets, drinking water (often off in late summer), no hookups. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Fir Creek Campground
note: Small first-come, first-served USFS campground in Bear Valley (Boise NF, Lowman RD) on Elk Creek at ~6,350 ft; vault toilet, no potable water; open mid-June-Sept. Access via gravel Bear Valley Rd (FS 579). Temporarily closed for hazard-tree removal per FS (2026). --Claude

name: Buttermilk Campground
note: USFS campground (Caribou-Targhee, Ashton/Island Park RD) on Island Park Reservoir; 2 single-family loops + a group loop (~55 sites), paved access with gravel spurs, RVs to 45-50 ft, one electric site, vault toilets, potable water, concrete boat ramp with docks. ~40% reservable (Loop B), remainder FCFS. --Claude

name: Meadow Lake Campground
note: High-elevation USFS campground (Salmon-Challis, Leadore RD) on 13-acre Meadow Lake at ~9,170 ft; 17 sites (13 single, 4 double), vault toilets, potable water; sites fit RVs to ~30 ft. Access 17 mi south of Leadore then gravel FS 002. Mostly first-come, first-served (a couple reservable online). Open ~July-early Sept. --Claude

name: Mosquito Flat Reservoir
note: Salmon-Challis NF (Challis-Yankee Fork RD), ~15 mi NW of Challis on the shore of 49-acre Mosquito Flat Reservoir. 11 sites with tables/fire rings, vault toilets, no drinking water; accommodates motorhomes/trailers to 32 ft. First-come, first-served (not on recreation.gov). --Claude

name: Spring Creek
note: Payette NF (Weiser RD), ~27 mi N of Weiser along Spring Creek under ponderosa pine at ~4,900 ft. About 12 sites (5 reservable + 7 first-come, first-served); tables, fire rings, vault toilets, drinking water; several sites fit RVs 22-32 ft. Reservable online (partial) plus FCFS. --Claude

name: Cabin Creek Campground
note: Payette NF (Council RD), West Mountains along the West/Middle Fork of the Weiser River, ~4 mi S of Council on US-95 then ~10 mi E on FSR 186. Two loops: north loop 12 standard sites, south loop 6 horse-friendly sites (open to any camper) - a general campground that offers stock sites, not equestrian-only. First-come, first-served (scan-and-pay on the recreation.gov app on-site); potable water by hand pump in the north loop, no hookups; typical season May 15-Nov 4. --Claude

name: South Fork Salmon River Campground
note: Boise NF (Cascade RD), near Warm Lake off FSR 474 with Chipmunk Creek running alongside. 11 drive-in sites in a scenic old-growth ponderosa pine forest (partial shade); potable water on-site, vault toilets, no hookups; open mid-May-mid-Sept. Appears first-come, first-served (not listed on recreation.gov). --Claude

name: Hawley Creek Lower Campground
note: Salmon-Challis NF (Leadore RD), ~8 mi SE of Leadore via Hwy 29, a county dirt road, and FSR 275 up Hawley Creek. 4 drive-in sites, first-come, first-served; potable water, vault toilet, no hookups; ~30 ft max RV; fishing in Hawley Creek and a small reservoir; opens ~May 15. --Claude

name: Amanita Campground
note: Small single-family campground on the west shore of Lake Cascade near Donnelly, Boise NF; ~10 sites on a gravel loop (some reservable, some FCFS), vault toilets, drinking water, no hookups; boat ramp at the neighboring Rainbow Point CG; some sites have lake views/shoreline access. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Trout Creek Campground
note: 5 primitive sites near Landmark in dense pine, Boise NF Cascade RD; fire rings/grills/tables and vault toilet, no potable water, no hookups; accessed by most vehicles on narrow, sometimes rough forest roads (FSR 579/413) near Johnson Creek; early June-late Sept; First-come, first-served (not on recreation.gov). --Claude

name: Kennally Creek Campground
note: 11 sites (incl. 9 trailer units) along Kennally Creek in mature forest, Payette NF; reached ~19 mi in on Paddy Flat Rd (gravel, narrow, bumpy in spots); central hand-pump water, fire pits/tables, vault toilet, no hookups; stock loading ramp/hitching rails just outside the entrance (general campground); First-come, first-served, 14-day limit. --Claude

name: Evergreen Campground
note: Payette National Forest campground on the Weiser River just off US-95, ~14 mi north of Council. 12 sites (3 tent-only) with paved parking spurs on gravel loop roads; vault toilets, drinking water. 5 sites reservable online, rest first-come, first-served. Weiser River Trail access on site. --Claude
